analysis.title: Capri Holdings (CPRI) F2Q27 Earnings Review: 2Q beat and FY27 raise; focus still on MK recovery
key_insights: CPRI reported F2Q27 adjusted EPS of $0.42 vs GS/FactSet consensus of $0.21. Sales fell -5.5% Y/Y (-4.9% ex-FX) vs GS/consensus of -9.0%/-8.1%.
About $20mn of wholesale shipments shifted from 3Q into 2Q. After adjusting for it, the sales decline was -7.8% vs consensus of -8.1%, so the sales beat was more modest.

FY27 adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $2.20 from $2.15 (GS/consensus $2.13/$2.11). Revenue guidance rose to ~$3.420bn from ~$3.4bn, and adjusted operating income guidance rose to ~$175mn from ~$170mn.

3Q adjusted EPS guidance of $0.95 was in line with GS/consensus of $0.94/$0.93. Sales guidance of ~$1.005bn and operating income guidance of ~$90mn were below consensus ($1.012bn/$1.019bn sales, $108.3mn/$109.6mn operating income).

Michael Kors sales fell -8.6% Y/Y (-10.6% after adjusting for timing) vs GS/consensus of -11.1%/-10.9%. Management cited sequential improvement each month through the quarter as fall product arrived and inventory constraints eased. Early TikTok Shop reads and select new styles drove incremental full-price selling.
Management targets a return to growth at Michael Kors in 4Q. GS wants to see continued Outlet recovery and momentum broadening beyond a few core franchises before gaining confidence in durability.

Jimmy Choo sales rose +11.5% Y/Y (+7.6% ex-timing) vs GS/consensus of +2.9%/+3.1%, led by the Americas and EMEA. The FY27 brand revenue outlook was raised to ~$650mn from ~$635mn, with the LSD% segment margin forecast unchanged.

2Q gross margin was 63.3%, up ~230bps Y/Y, above consensus of 63.0% but below GSe of 64.0%. Drivers were higher full-price sell-through, brand mix and lower Y/Y tariff rates. Adjusted EBIT margin was 3.8% vs GS/consensus of 1.4%.
FY27 share repurchase plan was raised to ~$300mn from ~$200mn. GS cut its diluted share count estimates accordingly.

GS raised FY27/FY28/FY29 EPS estimates to $2.22/$2.52/$3.05 from $2.13/$2.34/$2.82. The 12-month price target rose to $20 from $18 on a rolled-forward Q5-Q8 EV/EBITDA method at an unchanged 6.25x multiple. Rating stays Neutral, with 7.1% upside from $18.68.
Guidance assumes an incremental 10% tariff rate through July 24, 2026 and 10%-12.5% thereafter.

market_movers.rationale: Price target raised to $20 from $18 on a rolled-forward EV/EBITDA valuation and higher estimates after the 2Q beat and FY27 raise. Rating stays Neutral because Michael Kors execution and Outlet recovery are still unproven.

sector_views.rationale: GS rates CPRI Neutral and is incrementally more positive on the Michael Kors recovery path, but still wants evidence of durability.

earnings_insights: F2Q27 reported (10/30/2026) adjusted EPS $0.42 vs GS/FactSet consensus estimate $0.21.
F2Q27 reported sales -5.5% Y/Y (-4.9% ex-FX) vs GS/consensus estimates of -9.0%/-8.1%. Excluding the ~$20mn wholesale timing shift, sales were -7.8% vs consensus estimate -8.1%.
F2Q27 reported adjusted EBIT margin 3.8% vs GS/consensus estimate 1.4%. Gross margin 63.3% vs consensus estimate 63.0% and GSe 64.0%.

FY27 company guidance: adjusted EPS $2.20 (prior $2.15) vs GS/consensus estimates $2.13/$2.11. Revenue ~$3.420bn (prior ~$3.4bn) vs GS/consensus estimates $3.396bn/$3.401bn. Adjusted operating income ~$175mn (prior ~$170mn) vs GS/consensus estimates $165.7mn/$167.4mn.

3Q27 company guidance: adjusted EPS $0.95 vs GS/consensus estimates $0.94/$0.93. Sales ~$1.005bn vs GS/consensus estimates $1.012bn/$1.019bn. Operating income ~$90mn vs GS/consensus estimates $108.3mn/$109.6mn.
3Q27 brand guidance: Michael Kors revenue ~$830mn vs consensus estimate $844mn. Jimmy Choo revenue ~$175mn vs consensus estimate $175mn.
FY27 brand guidance: Michael Kors revenue ~$2.770bn (prior ~$2.765bn), Jimmy Choo ~$650mn (prior ~$635mn). Michael Kors segment margin forecast is unchanged at LDD%, Jimmy Choo at LSD%.
GS estimates (FY ending March): EPS $2.22 FY27E, $2.52 FY28E, $3.05 FY29E (prior $2.13/$2.34/$2.82). Quarterly GS EPS estimates are $0.95 for 12/26E, $0.17 for 3/27E and $0.46 for 6/27E.
risk_factors: Upside risks: faster sales recovery and growth, faster-than-anticipated margin recapture from improving brand heat, and stronger-than-expected cash flow generation.
Downside risks: a longer path to sales improvement, sustained margin compression, and balance sheet and FCF deterioration.
Execution risk on sustaining brand momentum and driving an inflection to growth in the Outlet channel.
Tariff rate assumptions embedded in FY27 guidance.

tension_points.bull_case: Sequential monthly improvement through the quarter, early TikTok Shop reads and new styles driving full-price selling, stronger profit control, a return to growth targeted for 4Q, and an increased buyback to ~$300mn.
tension_points.bear_case: Execution remains a key debate, including sustaining brand momentum beyond a few core franchises and driving growth in the Outlet channel. 3Q sales and operating income guidance came in below consensus.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A longer-dated path to sales improvement, or Michael Kors failing to return to growth in 4Q, with no continued Outlet recovery.
